correctness.rationale: The first three affine frequency rows have determinant 1, so phase modulation fixes them uniquely and preserves q-th roots. Parseval on probability Haar measure applies to the cubic Fourier expansion; an independent multinomial and Laurent-coefficient replay (python3 /workspace/review_replay.py hexagon) gave 37 buckets, with multiplicity histogram 6 of 1, 12 of 3, 12 of 6, 1 of 12 and 6 of 15. It exactly recovered the 21 Laurent terms of the displayed moment and counted two minimum gauges and one maximum gauge on the exact sixth-root grid. With r=u/v and s=w/v, express the Laurent sum as 564+144 Q+18(1+Q) Re(h) for Q=|1+r+s|^2 and h=vrs, giving both exact deficits. Lower equality forces r,s to be the two distinct primitive cube roots in either order and v=-1; upper equality forces r=s=v=1. The full phase torus is compact and connected, so the range is the entire closed interval. The free modulation action has size q^3 in the finite alphabet; the normalized minimizing representatives require primitive sixth roots. The finite replay is not used to infer a continuous optimum; that follows from the nonnegative identities. This is a continuous unit-modulus claim on this shell only, not unrestricted extension or an aliased-grid result.
